# Audio design: the Sound Forge + game-audio runtime

Status: design, 2026-09-30. It is based on three research passes: how shipped games structure audio, procedural sound
synthesis, and Web Audio best practice (sources at the end). This is the plan the arena's `audio.js` grows into.

**Goal:** every sound in the game is generated by our own code, with no sample library and no AI provider. It should
sound physical rather than "synthy", never repeat exactly, and be mixed and managed the way shipped games do it.

---

## 1. The big picture

```
 FORGE (what a sound IS)                RUNTIME (when / where / how loud)             TOOLING (is it good?)
 recipes: pure seeded DSP functions     event registry (data)                         forge CLI: WAV + spectrogram PNG
   modal / granular / bubbles /    ──►   containers (random, switch, blend, layer) ──►  + metrics JSON per variant
   friction / string / noise            voice manager (caps, priority, coalescing)    pass criteria per recipe
 baked at load in a Worker              buses → limiter, snapshots (ducking)          reference matching (analysis only)
 into N variants per event              spatial (pan, distance, LPF), reverb/biome    audition page + your ratings
                                        ambience (beds + scatterers + emitters)
```

Three separations borrowed from FMOD and Wwise:

- **Gameplay posts events, not sounds.** It calls `audio.post('arrow_hit', {x, y, material: 'stone', intensity: .8})`.
  Everything behind the name (recipe, variants, limits, bus, spatial behaviour) is data that can be tuned without
  touching gameplay code.
- **Content vs playback.** Recipes decide what a sound is. The runtime decides how often it plays, where, how loud and
  whether it may play at all.
- **Design vs verification.** I can't hear, so every sound also has measurable targets and a picture.

---

## 2. The Forge: recipes and the DSP kernel

### 2.1 Where the DSP runs

- **Our own small DSP kernel in plain JS** (`audio/forge/dsp.js`): biquads, one-pole filters, envelopes, band-limited
  oscillators, white/pink/brown noise, a two-pole resonator bank (modal), a Karplus-Strong string, a PhISEM particle
  model, waveshaping (tanh), DC-blocking, and a small Schroeder/FDN reverb.
- **Randomness:** everything is seeded with mulberry32, never `Math.random`.
- **Recipes are pure functions:**
  `recipe(params, seed, sampleRate) → {ch: [Float32Array], meta}`.
  They are deterministic and identical in the browser, a Worker and Node.
- **Why not Web Audio graphs or OfflineAudioContext for synthesis?** Measured here, the same graph renders 2–5 dB
  differently in Chrome and in Node Web Audio ports. OfflineAudioContext only runs on the main thread (spec issue
  #2423) and can stall it. Pure JS in a Worker ran **240 variants × 0.4 s in about 0.3 s** (≈313× realtime) in Node.
- **At load:** create the AudioContext early (it starts suspended) to read `sampleRate`. A Worker pool (1–2 workers)
  bakes variants in priority order: steps, hits, shots and UI first, rare sounds after. It transfers Float32Arrays, and
  the main thread wraps them with `createBuffer` + `copyToChannel`. Until an event's variants arrive, the current
  live-graph synth is the fallback. Optional cache in IndexedDB, keyed by `hash(recipeVersion, params, seed, sr)`.
- **Upgrade path:** if hand-written JS DSP becomes limiting, Faust compiled to WASM with an offline processor (LGPL,
  precompiled so the compiler doesn't ship). AudioWorklet is only for continuous sounds that react to gameplay, if
  node graphs get too heavy. No SharedArrayBuffer, because that would require cross-origin isolation headers.

### 2.2 Variants and memory

| Kind | Variants baked | Runtime jitter on top |
|---|---|---|
| Footsteps (per surface) | 6–8 | pitch ±1 semitone, gain −2..0 dB, avoid-last-2 |
| Arrow impacts (per material) | 4–6 | pitch ±1.5 st, gain −3..0 dB |
| Bow release | 4 | pitch ±1 st |
| Breakables | 3–4, plus a separate debris layer | pitch ±1.5 st |
| Explosion | 3 cores, plus random debris/tail layers | pitch ±1 st |
| UI / pickups | 1–2 | ±0.3 st or none (UI should stay consistent) |

- One-shots are **mono** (the runtime pans them). Beds and wide ambiences are stereo.
- Budget: ~40 events × 6 × 0.4 s mono ≈ 23 MB of float32; beds as 8–10 s stereo loops ≈ 3.7 MB each; ≈ 30–40 MB in
  total. Mobile: 4 variants and shorter tails, or Int16 storage.
- **Layering multiplies variety:** transient × body × tail chosen independently means 3 × 3 × 2 = 18 outcomes from 8
  buffers. The tail layer can switch per biome.

### 2.3 Recipe catalogue (models from the research; tune by measurement, then by ear)

**Principles:**
- **Decay time identifies the material more than pitch does.** Quality factor q = π·f·tₑ.
  Flesh/rubber 5–44, wood 15–130, glass 190–5000, steel 270–5000.
- **The noise residue** (the short filtered-noise attack) matters as much as the resonant modes.
- **Higher modes die faster.**
- **Glass and metal need near-duplicate modes detuned 0.5–3 Hz**, so they beat.
- **Contact time sets brightness:** a hard hit means a short τ_c, which is both brighter and louder.

| Sound | Model | Key numbers |
|---|---|---|
| **Impacts** (arrow → wood/clay/stone/crystal/straw/flesh) | Modal bank (10–30 modes) excited by a half-sine force pulse of duration τ_c, plus a noise residue | wood: beam ratios 1:2.76:5.40:8.93, f₀ 150–700 Hz, q 15–60; clay: 400–2500 Hz, q 30–120, gritty residue; stone: dense 1–5 kHz modes, q 5–30, mostly click + noise; crystal: 2–6 kHz, q 500–3000, beating pairs; straw/flesh: τ_c 3–15 ms, LP noise, no ringing. τ_c: stone 0.05–0.3 ms, wood 0.5–2 ms. Per hit: modes ±f/300, gains ±20%, strike position via sin(nπx/L). Arrow-in-wood adds a shaft "thrum" (80–250 Hz, 100–300 ms) |
| **Breaking** (crate, pot, barrel, crystal) | Crack burst + parent modes, then 5–40 fragments with power-law sizes (modes ∝ 1/size), scheduled with falling and bouncing physics | first landing after √(2h/g) ≈ 0.25–0.45 s, ±30–80 ms spread; bounces Δt·e with e: shards .3–.5, planks .4–.6, pebbles .6–.8. Crate: fibre-tearing clicks 1–5 ms apart, BP 1–6 kHz for 50–200 ms. Barrel: staves 80–250 Hz + metal hoop ring. Crystal: 20–60 high-q shards + 0.5–1.5 s tinkle |
| **Bow release** | Extended Karplus-Strong string + slap click + limb thump + departing whoosh | f₀ 90–220 Hz, pick position .1–.2, heavily damped (T60 60–250 ms: a bowstring is dead), pitch glide −3..−8% in 20 ms, slap 2–5 ms BP 2–4 kHz, limb modes 60–150 Hz |
| **Bow draw creak, chest hinge** | Stick-slip impulse train → wood formants (+ panel delays) | draw: 15→80 Hz over the draw, ±10–30% jitter; wood formants 62.5/125/250/395/560/790 Hz; hinge: 5–40 Hz, formants 400–2000 Hz; faint string-stretch HP noise −20 dB |
| **Arrow whoosh / flyby** | Aeolian tone (Strouhal) + broadband noise + fletching flutter + Doppler | f = 0.2·v/d, i.e. 750–1500 Hz for an 8 mm shaft at 30–60 m/s, BP Q 3–10, flutter AM 20–60 Hz |
| **Footsteps** | Ground-reaction-force exciter (heel → roll → toe, heel–toe gap up to 150 ms) drives a surface model; every step rendered differently | stone: heel modes 200–2500 Hz q 5–20 + noise, toe −6 dB 60–150 ms later, scuff 2–6 kHz; grass: PhISEM 200–1000 grains @ 2.5–5 kHz, low q + swish; gravel: 2–3 PhISEMs @ ~0.8/2.5/6 kHz; snow: PhISEM 1–4 kHz + crumpling micro-clicks + 1–2 kHz squeak, LP 5 kHz; crystal: glass-mode impact + sparse sleigh-bell grains. Landing: two heel events 10–30 ms apart, ×2–3 amplitude |
| **Roll / jump / climb** | Cloth whoosh (BP noise 0.4–1.5 kHz swept by a bell envelope over 200–400 ms) + body thumps; climbing = fractal-noise friction + grip clicks + debris trickle | |
| **Water: stream, splash** | van den Doel bubbles: f₀ ≈ 3/r (Minnaert), d = 0.13/r + 0.0072·r^−1.5, rising pitch f(t)=f₀(1+0.1·d·t); populations with power-law radii | stream: Poisson 50–500 bubbles/s, r 0.3–5 mm, plus a brown-noise gurgle (LP 300–600 Hz) and HP spray; splash: impact noise, then 20–200 bubbles over 50–400 ms, plus one big "plunk" bubble and drips 150–600 ms later |
| **Lava** | Big, heavily damped bubbles + pop + sizzle + sub rumble | f₀ 60–250 Hz, damping ×3–10, 0.5–3 events/s |
| **Fire / embers** | Farnell: hiss (HP noise × a slow random modulator raised to the 4th power) + crackle (≈20 ms bursts through resonant BPs 1.5–16.5 kHz) + lapping (BP 30 Hz, Q 5, clipped) | mix hiss .25 / crackle .2 / lapping .6; embers: sparse 4–12 kHz crackles |
| **Wind** | Pink/brown noise → BP 200–800 Hz driven by a peaky gust controller (0.05–0.5 Hz); whistles = narrow BPs (Q 30–150) that fade in above a speed threshold; leaves = HP noise with fast AM | decorrelated L/R |
| **Explosion** | 5 layers: Friedlander crack (1–5 ms) + boom (brown noise LP 40–150 Hz + sub sweep 60→30 Hz) + fireball roar (BP 200–800 Hz) + debris (fracture model) + tail; tanh glue | distance: more LP, lower direct-to-reverb ratio |
| **Metal** (coins, trap, latch) | Metal modal bank (10–30 inharmonic modes, q 300–5000) + bounce sequence; trap = spring coil ring + jaw impact (τ_c < 0.2 ms) + chain grains | coin ratios ≈ 1:1.73:2.33:3.91:4.11; loot chimes: bell partials tuned to a scale, ±1–2 cents |
| **Birds / crickets / owl** | Chirp syllables (glides 2–8 kHz, 20–150 ms, trill AM 10–40 Hz) arranged by a phrase grammar; crickets: 3–5 pulses of 10–20 ms on a 3–5 kHz carrier, chorus of 10–40 detuned individuals; owl: 250–900 Hz hoot, soft attack, glide + breath | |
| **Rift drone / whispers** | Detuned beating partials + slow filtered noise; whispers = noise through 3 vowel formants hopping at 3–6 syllables/s + fricatives | |

**Realism checklist** (why procedural SFX sound fake):
- never an identical repeat
- no bare sines or perfect exponential decays (always add a residue)
- sharp, varied transients
- pink/brown noise rather than white
- peaky random modulation and Poisson timing
- shared randomness for components that share a cause
- a short room on everything
- gentle tanh saturation
- HP filter at 30–60 Hz
- 1–5 ms fades
- judge sounds in the mix, not only solo

## 3. Runtime: how the game plays sounds

### 3.1 Event registry (data)
```js
arrow_hit: {
  bus: 'sfx.impacts', priority: 60, maxInstances: 5, steal: 'quietest', coalesceMs: 40,
  spatial: {minDist: 2, maxDist: 18, pan: .7, lpfFar: 4000},
  container: {type: 'switch', param: 'material', cases: {
    stone: {type: 'layer', children: [{type: 'random', avoidLast: 2, recipe: 'impact.stone', variants: 6},
                                      {type: 'random', recipe: 'debris.grit', variants: 3, gainDb: -6, delayMs: [0, 20]}]},
    wood: {...}, flesh: {...} }},
  pitchSemi: [-1.5, 1.5], gainDb: [-3, 0], baseGainDb: -4,
  rtpc: {intensity: {gainDb: [[0, -6], [1, 0]], pitchSemi: [[0, .5], [1, -1]]}},
}
```
**Container types:**
- `random` (with avoid-last-N)
- `shuffle` (bag)
- `sequence`
- `switch` (by a parameter)
- `blend` (crossfade by a parameter)
- `layer` (play all children, with offsets)

Each one is a pure picker returning `[{buffer, gain, rate, delay}]`.

**API:**
- `post(name, params)` → handle
- `setParam(name, value)`
- `setState(name, on)`
- `startLoop(id, emitter)` / `stopLoop(id)`

### 3.2 Voice manager
- **Global cap:** 32 physical voices on desktop, 20 on mobile. AAA consoles run 30–40 physical voices.
- **Per event:** `maxInstances` and a steal policy (`oldest | quietest | furthest | none`).
- **Priority:** 0–100, lowered by up to 20 at max distance. A new voice below the lowest active one is rejected.
  Otherwise the weakest voice is stolen with a 10–20 ms fade.
- **Coalescing (the "30 arrows at once" answer):** identical events within 30–50 ms merge into one playback, with
  +2 dB per doubling of the count (max +6 dB). From 5 merged events, switch to a "volley" variant.
- Cull any voice whose computed gain is under −40 dB before creating nodes.
- Keep per-event cooldowns and the existing same-sound attenuation.
- **Loops go virtual when inaudible:** stop the node and keep the clock. Restart at `elapsed % duration`.

### 3.3 Buses, mixing, snapshots
- **Master tree:**
  - Music
  - Ambience (Beds, Spots, Emitters)
  - SFX (Player, Enemies, Impacts, Breakables, Footsteps, World)
  - UI (dry)
- **Voice chain:** `BufferSource → gain → (lowpass if d > 3 m) → StereoPanner → bus`, plus a reverb send.
- **Master:** gain → DynamicsCompressor used as a limiter (threshold −3, ratio 20, knee 0, attack ~1 ms, release 100–250
  ms) → destination.
  - True peak ≤ −1 dBTP.
  - The limiter should rarely engage. If it works constantly, fix the gains.
- **Loudness targets:**
  - Each variant is normalised by momentary-max LUFS: short SFX are too short for integrated loudness, because of its
    gating.
  - Whole mix: −16 to −18 LUFS integrated on laptop speakers and earbuds. ASWG-R001 gives −24 for console and −18 for
    mobile.
- **Footsteps:** 10–14 dB under combat hits.
- **Snapshots:** named sets of target bus gains and filters, ramped with `setTargetAtTime`.
  - `explosionDuck`: music −4, ambience −6, released over 600 ms.
  - `hitstop`: non-player SFX −3 dB during the freeze.
  - `lowHP`: LPF about 2 kHz, plus a heartbeat.
  - `pause`: LPF 800 Hz, −6 dB.
  - `biomeTransition`: 2 s crossfade.
- **Optional "loudest wins"** (DICE HDR, simplified): each event has a loudness value. A 30 dB window follows the
  loudest active sound with about 1 s release. Quieter sounds are pushed down or culled, so explosions read clearly
  without hand-made ducking.
- **Optional importance mixing** (Overwatch): the most threatening enemy's sounds get about +7 dB. Other entities are
  quieter, high-passed and lower priority.

### 3.4 Spatial (top-down 2.5D)
- **Pan from the camera** (screen x). **Attenuate from the player.**
  - Equal-power StereoPanner, pan = clamp(dx / halfScreenW) × 0.7. Never hard-pan.
  - No HRTF: it is expensive and pointless for 2D.
- **Attenuation curve:** 0 dB within ~2 m, then −6 dB per doubling, culled at ~1.5× the screen half-diagonal.
- **Low-pass with distance:** 20 kHz → 3–5 kHz. Optional occlusion (−6 dB, 1.5 kHz) behind walls or cliffs.
- **Reverb:** one short convolver per biome (≤1.2 s, synthetic IR baked by the forge).
  - Sends: 10–20% on SFX; none on UI or music.
  - Crossfade two convolvers on a biome change. Don't swap `.buffer` live: Chrome prepares IRs on the main thread.

### 3.5 Gameplay systems
- **Footsteps:** triggered on animation contact frames (the player already emits them). Surface comes from what's
  under the foot, and walk and run are separate intensities. Low priority, max 2 per emitter.
- **Impacts:** a projectile × target material matrix. `intensity` comes from damage, crits or draw charge. Glancing
  hits are quieter.
- **Game feel:**
  - The hit sound starts on the damage frame, at the *start* of hitstop, with zero latency.
  - The bow draw is a creak whose rate and pitch follow the draw amount (a parameter), with a "full-charge" tick at
    max draw.
  - Release = string + slap + whoosh + a random shaft rattle.
  - The kill confirm is distinct, high priority and never stolen.
- **Ambience** (the standard 3-part system):
  1. Beds: 1–2 stereo loops per biome and time of day, so there is never total silence.
  2. Scatterers: random spot one-shots every 3–12 s, pan ±0.8, pitch ±1 st.
     - ruins: stone settle, birds / crickets, owl
     - ember: crackle, lava blurp
     - frost: ice creak, gust
     - rift: whispers
  3. Positional emitters: loops with attenuation, LPF and virtualisation (the stream).
- **Music** (later): 2–4 vertical stems per biome, combat stems driven by a `combat` state (the Hades approach).

### 3.6 Browser lifecycle
- **Unlock:** create the context early. On the first `pointerdown`/`keydown`, `resume()` it and start a 1-sample
  silent buffer synchronously (iOS needs this).
- **iOS:** handle the `"interrupted"` state by resuming again on `visibilitychange`, `focus` or the next gesture.
- **Hidden tab:** suspend while hidden (already done).
- **Sync:** use `outputLatency` when lining visuals up with audio.
- **Profiling:** Chrome DevTools' WebAudio panel shows render capacity.

## 4. Tooling: how a designer who can't hear keeps quality up

1. **Forge CLI** (`node tools/sfx/forge.mjs <recipe|all> [--seeds 6] [--case x]`; `--refs` measures the reference takes). For every variant it writes:
   - a `.wav` file
   - a **spectrogram PNG**: log-frequency, dB −90..0, with a waveform strip and a time grid
   - `metrics.json`: peak and true peak, momentary-max LUFS, attack time (10→90%), T60 per band, spectral
     centroid/spread/roll-off/flatness/flux, crest factor, onset density, DC offset, click check at the start and end,
     and similarity between variants

   It also writes a contact-sheet HTML covering all recipes.
2. **Pass criteria per recipe**, checked after every edit. Example `footstep.stone`: attack < 3 ms; centroid 1.5–3 kHz;
   T60 < 150 ms; variant similarity < 0.9. Golden tests check metric *ranges*. Exact bytes are checked only for the
   deterministic kernel.
3. **Reference matching** (analysis only; nothing ships):
   - Use CC0 recordings or our 12 ElevenLabs trial takes as targets.
   - Peak-pick mode frequencies and decays from them, which is how the modal research does it.
   - Optimise the parameters with random-restart hill climbing or CMA-ES. The loss combines multi-resolution STFT
     log-magnitude, MFCC, envelope, centroid and flatness.
   - Match against 3–5 references and take the median to avoid overfitting.
   - Textures (fire, stream, wind, crickets) are compared on McDermott–Simoncelli statistics: subband envelope
     moments and modulation power.
4. **Audition + rating page** (`assets/sfx/audition.html` grows into this):
   - Forge vs reference A/B rows, blind, with 1–5 realism ratings and notes.
   - Ratings export as JSON, which I read to decide what to tune next.
   - Every sound is also rated in context in the arena, because masking hides artefacts and exposes others.
5. **Headless Chrome over CDP** (Node 24 has a built-in WebSocket, so there are no dependencies) is the reference for
   anything that involves real Web Audio nodes, such as the master chain and level tests. `--dump-dom` does not wait
   for audio rendering.

## 5. Build plan

| Phase | Deliverable | Proves |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Forge core** | `audio/forge/dsp.js` kernel, the forge CLI (WAV + spectrogram + metrics), the audition/rating page. First recipes: impact (wood, clay, stone, crystal), crate break, bow release, stone footsteps, stream. A/B against the ElevenLabs trial takes | Procedural quality is good enough; the see-and-rate loop works |
| **2. Runtime** | Event registry, containers, voice manager, buses + limiter, spatial, Worker baking at load. Wired into the arena behind the existing `createAudio / update / toggle` contract, with the old synth as fallback | Game-grade playback: no machine-gunning, no clipping in chains |
| **3. Full catalogue** | All recipes in §2.3, the ambience system (beds, scatterers, emitters), biome reverbs, snapshots | Complete soundscape |
| **4. Mix pass** | Record 20–30 min of play, measure LUFS and true peak, tune bus gains, then event gains; mobile budget check | Consistent, comfortable loudness |

### Licensing notes
- Implement from the papers and books. Don't paste code from GPL projects such as the Sound Design Toolkit (read it
  only).
- Farnell's Pure Data effects bundle is CC-BY 3.0, so credit it if we port a patch closely.
- The "Designing Sound in SuperCollider" wikibook is CC BY-SA: its ideas are free to use, but copied code would carry
  the share-alike terms.
- STK (PhISEM presets) is MIT-style.

## Where things live (phase 1)

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `audio/forge/dsp.js` | DSP kernel: rng, noise, biquads, envelopes, oscillators, modal bank, Karplus-Strong, PhISEM, bubbles, bounces, Poisson, room |
| `audio/forge/metrics.js` | analysis: LUFS (momentary max), true peak, attack, T60, spectrum stats, onsets, similarity, criteria check |
| `audio/forge/spectro.js` | spectrogram image (waveform strip + log-frequency, absolute dBFS) for PNGs and canvases |
| `audio/forge/forge.js` | `bake(recipe, case, seed, sr)`: render → clean → normalise to -20 LUFS (-1.2 dB peak cap) → measure → check |
| `audio/forge/recipes/*.js` | one recipe per file; contract and registry in `recipes/index.js` |
| `audio/forge/lab.html` | listen, A/B blind against references, rate, export ratings (served at `/audio/forge/lab.html`) |
| `audio/forge/out/` | CLI output: WAV + PNG per variant, `summary.json` per recipe, `index.html` contact sheet |
| `audio/forge/refs/` | reference takes measured at the same loudness (analysis only; never shipped) |
| `tools/sfx/forge.mjs` | the forge CLI (Node 24, no dependencies) |

## Status

- **Phase 1 (forge core): built 2026-10-01, awaiting listening tests.**
  - 6 recipes: impact (wood / clay / stone / crystal / straw / flesh), crate_break (crate / pot / barrel), bow_release (basic / heavy / multi), footstep (stone / grass / gravel / snow / crystal / land_stone / run_stone), stream (brook / calm / rapids, seamless stereo loops) and splash (small / big / step).
  - All 168 variants (6 seeds × 28 cases) pass their criteria.
  - Similarity to the ElevenLabs references: wood 0.84–0.89, crate 0.87–0.90, bow 0.81–0.88, stone step 0.84–0.90.
  - Next: the user rates the sounds in `audio/forge/lab.html`, and exports `forge-ratings.json` for tuning.
- **Kernel candidates** reported by the recipe agents: currently local helpers inside the recipe files; promote them to dsp.js when reused.
  - `strike` / `contactTrain` / `contactForce` / `contactEnv` / `decayLen` / `tailFade` (impact.js)
  - material mode tables → `materials.js`
  - `clickTrain`, `tear`
  - `ksDamp`, `arrowWhoosh`, `gait` / `force` / `load` (the GRF), `band` (footstep.js / bow_release.js)
  - the circular loop toolkit: `fold`, `circBiquad`, `loopLfo`, `poissonT` (stream.js)
  - `addBurst`
- **Library expansion (2026-10-01):** 26 recipes, 436/436 variants pass, after two listening passes.
  - New families: combat (arrow_fly, arrow_stick, explosion, trap, stomp), character/loot/UI (cloth, bow_draw, coin, chest, magic, climb, ui), world (wind, fire, lava, rift, creature, ice, prop), plus `plunk` (the 5/5 splashes, kept by request).
  - After "white noise in every nature sound, everything too high", every recipe was darkened under the hard brightness rules in `audio/forge/RECIPE_GUIDE.md`.
  - `metrics.js` gained `hf4kDb` (energy above 4 kHz re total). All loop textures now sit at -22..-115 dB.
  - `dsp.js` gained `warm()`. The lab plays loops at -34 LUFS (ambience level) and one-shots at -24.
  - Renamed cases keep their old draws through `seedAs` (case) / `seedId` (recipe).
- **Phase 2 (runtime): wired 2026-10-01.** `audio/runtime/`: bakery.js + bake.worker.js (Worker baking, 2 workers), engine.js (bus tree + limiter, voices/coalescing/stealing, distance, reverb per biome, loops, snapshots), events.js (all 29 arena sound names → forge recipes, levels, limits, prefetch priorities, AMBIENCE beds/spots/emitters per biome×time), director.js (post / prefetch / ambience / continuous creak + roll).
  - `arena/audio.js` creates the runtime at load and tries `director.post()` first, falling back to its legacy synth. The legacy chain, the music and the forge all end in the forge engine's master. Forge beds take over from the legacy bed when baked.
  - `?forge=0` = legacy only, for A/B.
  - Live headless test: 88 banks baked in 6 s (69 MB); 25/25 gameplay sounds played from the forge, 0 fallbacks, 0 errors.
  - Contract and API: `audio/runtime/CONTRACT.md`. Gaps: no lava/rift plop one-shots, roll is chained one-shots, no crystal arrow_stick, no IndexedDB cache, Firefox/Safari untested.
- **Phase 3 (screen-bound ambience + gaps): 2026-10-01.** After the user's "too much happening that isn't on screen; random sounds in my ear":
  - audio.js passes `off` (metres beyond the view edge) with every sound, and the visible torches/braziers as `sources`.
  - events.js `SPATIAL` gives each event a category:
    - world: -6 dB per metre off-screen, cut at 2 m
    - combat: -3 dB per metre, cut at 6 m, plus a low-pass
    - player / ui: never touched
  - Random close spot calls are removed. Wildlife sounds only via the wildlife system's events. What remains are rare distant `calls` (≤ -30 dB, low-passed, panned wide; budget 2 per 10 s), plus a quiet insects bed.
  - Visible torches/braziers get fire emitters (4 nearest).
  - Ambience ducks with combat intensity; beds are 2.5 dB quieter.
  - Ambient one-shots per minute: night 29–31 → ~2, day 9 → 1–2.
  - New recipes: insects (night/dusk/day loops), prop_roll (stone/dirt loop; speed sets rate and gain), arrow_stick/crystal, splash/lava and splash/rift.
- **Phase 4 (loudness pass): 2026-10-01.** Measured with `node tools/sfx/mixmeter.mjs`, which taps the engine buses in the live arena. The user's report was "pretty damn loud ambience noise". The cause was MUSIC, not the beds: the idle pad (detuned sawtooth chords) played at -24 LUFS-M, about 25 dB over the wind bed and almost as loud as combat.
  - **Fixes:**
    - Music master 0.25 → 0.1; the idle (pad-only) state a further -4.4 dB.
    - Pads darker, with less detune (the beating read as buzz/noise); music reverb send .45 → .25.
    - Stream / lava / rift-crack emitters -4 dB; torch / brazier emitters -4 dB; rift drone -3.5 dB.
  - **Mix targets (momentary-max LUFS at master 100%)** and measured results after the fixes:

    | Layer | Target | Measured |
    |---|---|---|
    | combat SFX | -20..-22 | -22 |
    | music, exploring / combat | about -34 | -36.7 idle, -33 in combat |
    | ambience beds | -42..-50 | -44 ember, -48 ruins / frost, rift now about -45 |
    | stream at the bank | about -40 | -40 |
    | fires | about -44 | -44 |
    | idle mix | about 14 dB under combat | -36 |
  - **Open:** the absolute level. Integrated play loudness is about -27 LUFS, quieter than the web norm of -16..-18. If the user wants the whole game louder, raise the forge engine's master: the limiter handles peaks.
